method: A drumhead is modelled as an ideal circular membrane of radius a clamped at the hoop, carrying a uniform tension T in newtons per metre and an areal density sigma in kilograms per square metre. The transverse wave speed is c = sqrt(T / sigma) and the natural frequencies are f(m,n) = alpha(m,n) c / (2 pi a), where alpha(m,n) is the n-th positive zero of the Bessel function J(m): alpha(0,1) = 2.404826 for the fundamental, alpha(1,1) = 3.831706, alpha(2,1) = 5.135622 and alpha(0,2) = 5.520078 for the next three modes, so the overtones sit at about 1.59, 2.14 and 2.30 times the fundamental rather than at whole-number ratios. The page solves that relation both ways: from a tension it reports the fundamental and the three overtones, and from a target frequency f it reports the tension T = sigma (2 pi a f / alpha(0,1))^2 that produces it. The wave speed, the fundamental, the nearest equal-tempered note with its offset in cents (A4 = 440 Hz) and the total radial force around the rim, T times the circumference, are reported with them. The diameter is the playing diameter inside the hoop and may be entered in inches, centimetres or millimetres; the film weight is the areal density in grams per square metre, about 249 for 7 mil, 356 for 10 mil and 498 for 14 mil clear PET film, and it is converted to kilograms per square metre internally. Diameters are limited to 2 to 40 inches (50.8 to 1,016 mm), areal density to 50 to 2,000 g/m2, tension to 1 to 50,000 N/m and target pitch to 20 to 20,000 Hz; a target pitch whose tension would fall outside that band is refused with the reason instead of being reported, which is why 20 kHz is unreachable even on a 2 inch head of the lightest film. The model is the ideal membrane and not a real drum: the trapped air under the head adds mass, the film's bending stiffness, the collar and the glue ring stiffen the edge, and the tension is never perfectly uniform, so a real head sounds a few percent higher than the figure here. The tension is the membrane tension per unit length, not a lug torque, a DrumDial reading or a tuning recipe, and the page computes one head at a time with no shell, air cavity or two-head coupling.

sources.title: Vibration of a circular membrane - an ideal drumhead is a circular membrane of uniform thickness under tension attached to a rigid frame, the wave speed is c = sqrt(N_rr* / (rho h)) for the membrane tension and density, and the normal modes have angular frequencies omega_mn = alpha_mn c / a with alpha_mn the n-th positive zero of the Bessel function J_m

Bessel function - Bessel functions describe the radial part of the vibrations of a circular membrane and give the modes of a thin circular membrane such as a drumhead, and the zeros of J_0 occur at approximately 2.40483, 5.52008 and 8.65373
